newsitem.title: ANGOLA: Brazil says wants to increase share in Angolan oil.
newsitem.headline: Brazil says wants to increase share in Angolan oil.

text.p: Brazil's Petroleo Brasileiro (Petrobras) chief Joel Mendes Renno said on Monday the company wanted an increased share of Angola's oil wealth and had proposed to explore in deepwater fields on bloc 21.
Renno was part of a Brazilian delegation who accompanied Brazilian President Fernando Henrique Cardoso on a 24-hour visit to Angola which ended on Monday.
Petrobras, which began its operations in Angola in 1979, currently holds a 27.5 percent share in production on offshore bloc two with partners Texaco, Sonangol and Total.
The bloc, around the northern town of Soyo, produces 110,000 barrels per day (bpd) of which Petrobras takes 30,000 bpd.

"This has shown reasonable revenues but we think this is very little, considering we have been working here for more than 20 years and so it is necessary that we increase our presence in Angola," Renno told Reuters.
"We have told the minister of petroleum (Albina Assis) that Petrobras has much bigger potential and capacity to be present in Angola side by side other companies like we have in other countries.
"We have offered a proposal this morning to participate in a new bloc (bloc 21) in deepwater fields which is our speciality as recognised by Sonangol through European companies," he added.
Renno said at Monday's meeting with Angolan petroleum officials the company had also shown interest in onshore drilling and natural gas projects.

"Two years ago we made a proposal for a joint action project in natural gas. We have talked about this again during our meeting and they were interested and they have asked us to be patient because the country is being reorganised after having been through a difficult time," he said.
He said Brazil currently imported two million tonnes of natural gas a year, mainly from Saudi Arabia.
"If we can have a project with Angola it will be more convenient," he said.
Renno said Angola, which currently produces about 720,000 barrels per day, had enormous potential for development in the oil sector.
"We don't know what the oil reserves of Angola are but we know it is seen as an important oil producing country," he said.
Figures show that oil is Angola's main export to Brazil was worth $18.5 million in 1995, rising to $92.1 million this year.
